failures.assertion: Runs the command shape web2md 'https://example.com/guide' --out ./guide.md.web2md-tmp (a temporary path beside the requested ./guide.md, not the final path), with the URL and the output path as separate quoted arguments and no string interpolation, then validates the temporary file and publishes it as ./guide.md
failures.evidence: The output uses “web2md 'https://example.com/guide' --out "$tmp"”, interpolating a variable rather than supplying the required literal quoted temporary path.

failures.assertion: Confirms page identity: the title matches when one is available, otherwise the URL's host and the visible heading are checked
failures.evidence: The output says to verify that “its title, URL, and substantive body identify the requested guide,” but does not specify title matching or the host-and-visible-heading fallback.

failures.assertion: Applies the pass rule before keeping the result: a heading plus several sentences of body that is not a login, consent, error or navigation-only page; rejects login, consent, error and navigation-only output instead of reporting it as the page
failures.evidence: Although the output excludes “a login page, consent wall, error, or navigation-only output,” it never requires a heading plus several sentences of body before publication.

failures.assertion: Explains that persistent network activity beyond the idle threshold can keep the default networkidle2 from settling, without claiming it never settles
failures.evidence: The output only says "This avoids waiting for network idle and allows a bounded two seconds for rendering," without explaining how persistent network activity can prevent the default networkidle2 threshold from being reached.

failures.assertion: Copies the CLI's stderr message about Chrome not being found into the report
failures.evidence: The output says "The exact stderr text was not provided, so I cannot reproduce it verbatim" rather than copying the CLI's stderr message.

failures.assertion: Stops without retrying and without another browser automation stack
failures.evidence: Instead of stopping after the blocker and flag guidance, the output proposes another invocation: "web2md 'https://example.com/docs' --print --chrome-path \"$CHROME_PATH\"".

failures.assertion: Notes that a directory path means one file per URL
failures.evidence: The output offers “separate files in a directory” but does not explicitly explain that a directory path means one file per URL.

failures.assertion: Points to the dedicated --user-data-dir path only if the user wants it, and does not reuse the user's daily browser profile or use --no-sandbox
failures.evidence: Although the output says, “If you want to proceed, approve a dedicated browser profile for authentication—never your daily browser profile,” it does not identify the dedicated --user-data-dir path.
